newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: TRI to buy anti-phone fraud equipment.
newsitem.headline: TRI to buy anti-phone fraud equipment.

text.p: Malaysia's Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) on Friday signed agreements to buy equipment to curb fraudulent use of its analogue cellular phone system, a crime which has nibbled away at its profits.

The "cloning" of users' telephone numbers remains a threat to the company with 5,000 suspected fraud cases unearthed in the first six months of 1997, officials told reporters after the signing ceremony.
They said the cloning of its subscribers' phone numbers cost the company millions of ringgit but did not give any specific figures.
In such acts, criminals use sophisticated equipment to "clone" phone numbers which are then usually sold to foreign workers who rack up expensive phone bills calling home.
The company is forced to pick up the tab as the legitimate subscriber will refuse to pay for calls he or she did not make.
TRI's analogue network has a subscriber base of some 760,000, the largest in Malaysia.
TRI chairman Tajudin Ramli said the company last year set aside some 103 million ringgit, or 6.2 percent of its turnover, for bad debt provisions, against 44 million ringgit in 1995.
Company officials declined to give a figure for bad debt provisions this year, but said the industry average is between 7.0 and 10 percent.

TRI's new hardware and software costing 8.0 million ringgit will be supplied by Ericsson Telecommunications Sdn Bhd, Digital Equipment (M) Bhd and Pernec Corp Sdn Bhd. This is in addition to the 5.0 million ringgit anti-fraud system already in place.
